utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. I'm going to ask the registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning everyone in the court. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this Tuesday, the 16th of October, 2007, the Chamber wishes to greet representatives of the Prosecution, the ladies and gentlemen of the Defence counsel, and the accused. I do not wish to omit our interpreters who are assisting us. It was my understanding that Mr. Scott needed a few minutes to intervene. Mr. Scott, I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning to each of Your Honours. Good morning to all those in and around the courtroom. Just one moment just to clarify something that was said yesterday. On the 10th of October at -- 2007 at page 23609 of the transcript last week, the Prosecution specifically asked for leave to reply to the Heliodrom 92 bis motion reply filed -- response filed by the Defence and also a document motion involving some 398 documents. At that time, and Mr. Karnavas speaking at least for himself, if not the Defence as a whole, indicated there was no objection from the Defence side, and after the Chamber consulted with each other the Judges consulted with each other our request was granted. That request was not, not a request for extension of time to file a request for leave to reply, it was the request for leave to reply and to file our response by the 22nd of October. That motion was granted and we've gone forward on that basis. Your Honour, it's not -- if I can be very transparent and candid, the Prosecution does not have the time, despite other things that are sometimes said in the courtroom, the Prosecution does not have resources or time to waste on filings that are not going to be received. That's why we asked for permission, leave, before we spend the time, the days and hours to prepare a document. And, Your Honour, that's why we've asked for it, that's why we think it would be appropriate. We understand that there are times when there are written motions. The practice has been in some instances to file written motions, but at the same time there is no motion in the rules that cannot be made orally. All parties, the Defence, the Prosecution at times have made oral submissions in the interest of efficiency. Everyone is very busy right now, both the Prosecution and the Defence, and, Your Honour, again Prosecution -- I'm certainly not interested in having my team to spend time on preparing filings that will not be accepted. We think the Chamber will be assisted by our filing. Both filings are substantial. One involves the Heliodrom 92 bis motion with a number of witnesses involved. The document motion involves 398 documents. The Defence have made specific responses on a document by document basis in most instances. Of course the Prosecution can't know, the Prosecution cannot know the Defence objection, specific objections, particular objections, until the Defence filing is made and it's only now that we can make a reply to those particular objections. We think with all respect we should have the opportunity to do so. We also submit that it will assist the Chamber. The Chamber I would hope would find itself assisted by as much information on these matters as possible. So, Your Honour, I just wanted to clarify the situation. We ask for leave to file our reply to both Defence responses on Monday, the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could be of assistance, Mr. President. That was my understanding as well, which is why I said if it was up to me I would -- I would grant the motion. So I concur with Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. Regarding this procedural issue, the Chamber, which was orally informed of a request for an extension of time, after reviewing the matter realised that after this oral request you did not indicate the exceptional circumstances motivating the right to reply, because as you know, we have already decided to prevent responses except in exceptional circumstances, and these exceptional circumstances need to be indicated and elaborated. As you said quite clearly, this is a motion. This was pursuant to 92 bis concerning 398 documents. The Defence has replied, and you wish to respond in relation to the position of the Defence, and it is this response that we wish to justify by exceptional circumstances. That is what the whole debate is about. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have to say I find that particular rule not just this Chamber, that particular rule in general, to be one of the most annoying and I think unjustified rules of the Tribunal. It seems to me quite a silly rule that each party whether it's the Prosecution or Defence, the moving party, in virtually every system I'm aware of has a right to reply, and I thought this rule in this institution was quite misguided. Having said that, Your Honour, I think I just indicated what I believe the justification, whatever you want to call it, exceptional circumstances, justification are. These are voluminous motions. It involved a lot of effort on all sides including the Defence. The Prosecution cannot know what the Defence positions will be until the Defence filings are made. There have indeed been a number of instances in the past where once objections have been made positions have been modified, some exhibits have been withdrawn, redactions have been made, et cetera. We cannot do that until we have the specific Defence reply. So we believe, Your Honour, that there is justification, call it exceptional or not, but there is justification for the Chamber to receive the Prosecution's submissions, that the Chamber would be assisted by the Prosecution's submissions, and these very voluminous and somewhat complex filings. That's our basis for justification. That's our basis for asking for -- to file our replies on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have just further explained the exceptional circumstances. So let us now continue with the cross-examination of the witness. We will bring the witness in, who is waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. While that's happening, though, I must with all respect persist. My point is I'm not going to have our lawyers prepare submissions, spend days preparing submissions that will not be accepted. So I'm asking for a ruling from the Court so that I can assign my resources efficiently and prudently to prepare a submission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll tell you shortly. After we resume the hearing, we will inform you of our decision and ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Commandant. I hope you had a good evening last night. Your cross-examination will be continued now this morning, and I therefore give the floor to Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and for time purposes, time allocation purposes, I understand I used I think 21 -- 29 minutes, 29 minutes yesterday, so I have 31 minutes left of my own. I have all of Mr. Pusic's time and all of Mr. Coric's time so I believe it will be this session plus a little bit into the next session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. How are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I trust you had a restful evening?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not too bad. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did we take our jog in the morning?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in the afternoon hopefully today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Now I'm going to ask that you slow down, pause, because the interpreters yesterday had a very difficult time. I'm to blame partly but some blame rests on you as well, so please pause. Now, I want to go back to where you more or less ended yesterday on direct and pick up on that issue with respect to the map versus the chart or the drawing. Okay? Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I just want to make sure because representations were made by Mr. Stringer, the Prosecutor, where he indicated, and I quote: "What I can tell the Trial Chamber is that we informed the Defence by letter over the weekend of the change or correction, if you will, to the witness statement. So counsel was informed about it yesterday." That's what Mr. Stringer represented to counsel and to the Trial Chamber. Let me finish my question, sir, before you intervene. Now, in looking at what I received on 14 October 2007, I see that there are corrections to 16 paragraphs, 11 different entries. They have references to the paragraphs, but to the paragraph in question, which I believe is paragraph 47, there is no entry. So my question, sir, is: When did you bring this to the -- to the Prosecutor's attention?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there an objection? If there's an objection, I'd like to know the basis for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I was mistaken when I told the Trial Chamber yesterday that that item was included in the letter that went to the Defence, and I apologise for the mistake. This particular issue is in my letter. It's obviously not in the witness's letter. My letter to the Defence did not include this change or clarification, whatever you want to call it, in his witness statement. So I was mistaken when I said that, Mr. President. I didn't have the letter with me, and I apologise to the Trial Chamber and also to counsel for that, because it was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Apology accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's stick with this a little bit then. When you met with the Prosecutor, according to your testimony yesterday, you indicated that a drawing was shown to you, and I'm referring to page 99 for those who wish to refer to yesterday's transcript, and it begins more or less on -- the question is on line 13, but you said that "Yes, it was a drawing. I said before it was a map. In fact, it was just a simple drawing of a circle with a line down through the middle, and on one side we had Muslims, and on the other side we had Croats." And as you said, the Muslims -- sorry, you correct yourself, "Sorry, and the Serbs and the third party were not there." And I think from reading this, what you were trying to convey, if I'm not mistaken, that there was a circle. On the one side you got Croats, on the other side you got Serbs, and there was nothing there for the Muslims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me walk back with -- take you back to the time that you gave your statement. Your statement was given, as I understand it, over a two-day period back in, if I can get it here for a second, back in -- on the 25th and 26th of May, 2004; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I ask where that statement was, where you physically were at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Army headquarters in Dublin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you were in your home country.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ireland, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so you weren't going anywhere?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As in?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Like you were in a hurry in a sense?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You weren't pressed for time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was busy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, we're all busy.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're all busy, exactly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you managed to set aside two days and in fact, if the Prosecutor wanted a third day certainly, surely, the Irish military would have allowed you to have one extra day to sit with the Office of the Prosecution investigators?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My point being that you were not in a rush.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You spoke English?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I speak English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were speaking at the time English?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you were doing your interview?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And even though you were speaking with a Dutch investigator working for the office of the Prosecution, he spoke English as well?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You understood his English?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact he speaks fluently?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excellent. Okay. So there was no miscommunication, nothing lost in translation as they would say. You're shaking your head?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Remember, we have to pause, okay? Now, I take it before he arrived he informed you what the nature of his visit was.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he told you, perhaps, exactly what he was interested in discussing in detail. In other words, he gave you topics or at least the substance of what he wanted you to think about, maybe even look at your own records, see if you had any documents, so you could prepare in advance of his arrival; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. What I -- what I was told to prepare was my experiences from the period of time I served as -- as part of the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did he ask you to prepare a written document, something that you would submit to him as your faithful account of the events as you had remembered them, or was it simply for you to review some documents, think about it, let it brew in your head, and perhaps when he came you would just simply have a question-answer session with him?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The latter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The latter. Okay. And in the meantime, you had an opportunity to look at the indictment as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you define what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you knew that the reason that he was asking you to be interviewed was with respect to a particular indictment that had been issued by the Office of the Prosecution; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't actually remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you read the indictment?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Does that mean possibly yes, possibly no?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly yes, possibly no, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did he in advance advise you of the personalities that he was interested in discussing with you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But at some point you did read the indictment?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: At some stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this interview was not tape recorded?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Even though I suspect that tape recorders were available in case the Office of the Prosecution had failed to pack it along with his other ten essentials, a tape recording would have been available compliments of the Irish army in the event he wished to have a precise account of what questions were asked and what answers were given?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine. It's matter for him, not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm just asking you.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was there a tape recorder available?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything's available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it he never made the suggestion of tape recording it and neither did you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He certainly didn't make the suggestion. I didn't either, because I presumed that he was the expert at what he was doing and this was the SOP procedure. The standard operational procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay, and so over a period of two days you had a conversation with him, and afterwards he presented you with a document which was purportedly what exactly you had told him, a faithful, true, accurate, and complete account of all of the events which you had discussed.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, remember I asked you before whether you had an opportunity, whether you were in a rush, and you said no. If you needed an extra day, surely the army would have given you that extra day. So my question is: Did he give you an opportunity to read the statement which he had typed up as your account prior to you -- or did he give you an opportunity to read it? Let's --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the purpose for reading it was to make sure it was true, accurate, and complete; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, he probably told you - and if he didn't shame on him - but he probably told you that if you find any errors, correct them.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if you remember anything that you failed to mention, mention it so that it can be incorporated.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I take it you read it.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you're a military officer. You're shaking your head.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Karnavas, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you're a military officer, and I suspect that you have subordinates?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you have superiors?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as I understand it, superiors issue orders; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And subordinates occasionally, depending on their position, may have to write reports and to send them up to their superiors.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And over the period of your distinguished career as a military officer, you have -- you've had the occasion to do both. In other words, write reports for your superiors, issue orders to your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take when you do write a report or you do issue a order, you sign it.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you sign it or before signing it you make sure, because you are a meticulous man, I can just see that even just from the way you dress, that you make sure that what you are signing, because you are putting your imprimatur on that, you're vouching for the authenticity and the reliability, the veracity of everything that is in that document, you read it carefully to make sure that it is true, accurate and complete; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it because of your long-standing practice, your experience and the type of person who you are, you did that in this instance?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, in fact, the procedure as such as I understand it and as we can see from the statement, that with each page after reading it you initial it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's what you did in this case?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And after reading it thoroughly you signed it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And might I say one more thing. Is it possible that the gentleman, Mr. Spork, who wrote this out and which you proof-read and signed as being a true, accurate, and complete version of the events, did he say to you by any chance, "Mr. Lane, if you think of anything later on, don't hesitate to bring it to our attention. Here's my visiting card"?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recollect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Might I say that, however, being the person that you are, had you come up with anything new after reminiscing and going over these events, you would not have hesitated to contact the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I signed that document, my experiences in 1992 were probably dramatic as you probably gauged from me. When I signed that document in 1992 there was some closure in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I felt quite relieved at finally putting something on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But that's not my question though. And you're eating up my time.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My question is: Had something new popped into your mind, like you said, you were jogging in Scheveningen, it was probably a lovely day --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer your question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: See, there you go. It's not too difficult. Now, there are reasons why I'm asking you this, because at least to start with, as I indicated before, there were 16 paragraphs of which you wanted to make corrections to, and 11 different entries, starting with, starting with, and this is what caught my attention, to be honest, you know, and I'm a little concerned here, is starting with your own rank. You were put down as a commander. You signed it that that was a true, accurate and complete description of your rank, and yet now you say to us that you are a commandant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. There is a distinction. Otherwise, would you not have made that correction; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My rank is commandant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But obviously you didn't pick that when you -- picked that up when you were reading, proof-reading this.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that might account why there was some other errors as well?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I'd like to make a comment about that. I was aware that when I came here to proof-read over the weekend I thought the purpose of the proof-read was to do what I did do, find errors that might have been in the document that I might have missed back in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, how could you miss -- I mean, I've got to tell you how can you miss --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- your own rank?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or maybe I decided at that particular time that it wasn't a major issue and to leave it as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you told us earlier that he gave you the opportunity to read it to make sure that it was accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, but I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I might have considered it not that important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, okay, fair enough, fair enough. I'm going to skip ahead a little bit because I want to get where we started off because there are some other issues in this particular document, but I want to go to paragraph 47. And first I'm going to focus on the very narrow issue that we talked about. Yesterday, you told -- you told us under oath that you recall that you were shown a drawing of a circle, and it was just for Croats and Serbs. In your statement, you say on paragraph 47, I'm just going to read the relevant portion: "In discussions I held with Mr. Prlic at the time indicated -- at the time indicated his view on this tactic. He showed me a map of Bosnia and Herzegovina divided in half with little room for the Muslim population." Now, let's dissect this a little bit. You're saying after proof-reading this that he showed you a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not a drawing; correct? That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, and you're a military man and as I understand it I haven't served in the military, I wish I had, but I haven't, but as I understand, folks like you have a deep and abiding appreciate for maps.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's quite true. Officers don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you don't?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm in jest. They say one of the most dangerous things that you can find is an army officer with a map in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I mean, that's something that would stick out to you if you were looking at this map. That's why I mentioned it, you see?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You see, we're getting somewhere. And here you say it was divided in half with little room for the Muslim population and at least from -- when I read it seems at least this map, assuming it existed and assuming that this -- this indeed occurred with Mr. Prlic and not somebody else, and we'll get to that, over here it says, at least the way I read it, that there was some room for the Muslim population. So it wasn't just half for the Serbs, half for the Croats. You're shaking your head?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it this was -- you're claiming that this -- when you say that this meeting took place you don't recall when it occurred.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You claim that -- you believe that it occurred in his office.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was -- this would have been the office in the Ero hotel or --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- this is the other place.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rondo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was anybody with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's a yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Hold on.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was anybody with you at the time? Now there not too many possibilities in the universe of answers?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I feel --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I feel there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You feel?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Is that sort of like I don't know, perhaps, maybe, take a guess?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe I could say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, you answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ask me the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say you feel, okay, is that in other words you're saying I don't know, I don't recollect?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I'm saying is I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So it could be either one. Either, yes, there was or either no, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Yet, you recall this vividly after jogging on the beach you recall, you know, the map versus the drawing but yet you don't recall whether somebody was present in the room?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I don't think the witness was able to give his answer to the last question there. He started to say well and then was cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well -- well, I paused and allowed him -- there was a pause and it was pregnant.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said to you yesterday due to these proceedings here and the questioning, obviously parts of the brain that have been dead for many years in relation to Bosnia come alive again, and yesterday while I was considering this I remembered that we had a visit in Bosnia or in Herzegovina from a journalist from the BBC called Orla Guerin. Orla Guerin was taken by me to visit Mr. Prlic, and in that discussion this question of the map or the drawing came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I just want to make a point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So not?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just a second please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The events I'm talking about happened 15 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My point.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15 years ago is a long time. As I said a lot of water went under the bridge since then and as going through this procedure things are coming into my mind that I've forgotten about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other areas of particular interest which are not discussed in my testimony have come to the fore in the last day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, all right, point made. You made it yesterday, you made it again today. Let's hope that we don't have to make it again.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a very important point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right well I understand your memory is like fine French wine. It gets better with time, it seems to me.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife thinks my memory doesn't get better with time. It goes the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's my point as well.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, now. When you gave this statement to Mr. Spork, did he ask you for this map? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well don't you think if he was a good investigator he would say, well, did you get a copy of the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I missed the foundation. Did the witness ever possess this paper? Did he take it along? Was it ever in his hands?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going step-by-step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: No. You are jumping ahead because you're asking him whether he was asked to give it along. I think you are jumping a bit but...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you for those instructions but as I've indicated -- anyway I don't want to -- I don't want to get into a debate, Your Honour, you seem to constantly wish to instruct me on cross-examination and I take those instructions very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This map or drawing, did you ever ask, I was going to get there but let me get to it now, did you ever ask Mr. Prlic to give it to you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And is there a particular reason why you didn't ask Mr. Prlic to give you this drawing, especially if it was a drawing, a mere drawing, did you ask him especially since - let me finish - one of your jobs, one of your tasks, at least what you have claimed, was to provide information to your superiors?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't. Again, from what I remember I didn't ask for it and I didn't try and procure it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I take it, however, since this was vital information, at least vital enough to give it to Carry Spork and then have your memory revived on the beaches of Scheveningen to make the change that it wasn't a map but rather a drawing, that this would have been important information that you would have wanted to sure with your superiors, so obviously you must have put this into one of your reports?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you produce it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't, and as I said yesterday, part of my function was to produce weekly reports from my office back to RC Split which I did every week. I don't know where these reports are. I do not have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So I take it the best that we have is your account, what might have been a four eyes, four ears meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where we stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And just one last point, I know you didn't ask for the map or the drawing, we don't have any report, but I'm just curious, as meticulous as you are in writing reports and in issuing orders, not being rushed, how is it that you didn't pick up this piece of information, this -- this change? How is it that you could confuse a map of a country with a simple drawing with a circle on it? How is it that you didn't pick it up back then?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know whoever said I was meticulous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I thought you admitted that.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you said I was meticulous. You said I appeared --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so you're saying --?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that but I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what are you saying?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're saying I'm meticulous and you don't know me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you withdrawing that? Are you denying that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not. I'm just saying it's interesting to hear a person who doesn't know me make that comment about me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, are you or are you not?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meticulous?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm professional army.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means I do my job to the best of my ability in a professional manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay all right. Now let's move on a little bit. And I want too talk to you a little bit about this report. So let's just stay with this -- this paragraph because I want -- I was also curious when you said that in the beginning of it during the period "the self-styled government of Herceg-Bosna". Were those your words or were those the words of Mr. Spork?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they -- that term was actually used in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Used by whom?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the EEC -- by the European Community Monitoring Mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that means you would have been using that as well?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, well, could you please - I know we touched on it yesterday - but could you please describe how the self-styled government functioned, since you were there and you were supposed on it monitoring this self-styled government?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you -- can you expand on your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you claimed that it was self-styled because that's what you dubbed it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You said it was a government?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't dub it that that's the terminology that was used in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, well, your organisation dubbed it; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep, yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You got a briefing before you went in country?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, granted yesterday you told us for all intents and purposes there was no briefing other than there's the way to Bosnia, good luck; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in fact in your statement the briefing was all about more or less a -- a turf battle between you and this other gentleman as to who would head the mission?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's the way you read it or if that's the way it came across, that's not actually the truth of the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, but getting back to paragraph 47?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You chose these words "self-styled government of Herceg-Bosna". So we talk of -- we have three things that I'm interested in talking about. One, the word "self-styled" or that term "self-styled". Second, government. Third, Herceg-Bosna. Okay, so one would imagine that if the organisation you were working for and is using these terms and you were in a sort of a leadership position, albeit not at the very top, but you were nonetheless you were managing folks, and you were there and you want to describe to the -- to this court what exactly you learned and we're going to get to that, what is your understanding of the self-styled government of Herceg-Bosna? What is your -- how does it work? What is it? Where is it? What do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The from what I garnered on the ground, the HVO, the HVO were a political/military organisation which attempted to govern the entity that -- that the Bosnian Croats lived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to me that the -- that the people at the top of this organisation, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, and the rest were the leaders in this organisation and were directing the lives, if you like, of these people, of the Bosnian Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did they give you a map?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did who give me a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The ECMM. Did they give you a map of where Herceg-Bosna is because you said entity?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so I take it they must have given you a map to say, by the way, when you go into country just so you know here are the borders of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember did we get a map or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ask for one?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Again I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you think you might have asked for one being the nature?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Being the nature of the --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I'm going to go to another paragraph, so we're going to stick with this whole notion [Realtime transcript read in error "motion"] of government and what it means. You indicated yesterday that one of the first persons you met was Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In fact you said and I have it here, it's on page 28, "I met Mr. Boban in Grude with the mayor of Grude, Maric, Jozo Maric," and I see that in your statement you couldn't remember the gentleman's name, I take it --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- that's one of the things that came back to you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you said, yep, in fact he possibly was -- "as a mark of respect to him I think he was the first person I went to visit"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: You said probably that on page 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 28, line 22 there was starting with line 20, Your Honour. I can read the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Because I do not find 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Of the transcript yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry, talking about the transcript, I think you were talking about the whole page 26, line 14. The whole notion of government like in Nick and not like in madam, notion of government here it reads motion and that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Notion, notion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Notion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, and then you say out of respect he was the first person to visit. Then the next question is: "Do you recall at this point what his functional role was?" That's the question. I'm pausing here. Answer: "Except -- no, but he was obviously the important man."

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I want to make sure I understand this correctly. Somebody must have told you go see Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's an important man.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did that person, whoever that person might have been or wherever you got this information, did they tell you go see Mate Boban because he is the man?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- yes, I can see your point. I think by virtue of the fact that I went to see him first would indicate that he was the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, one would presume that since you were there to gather information both about the political and military structures and the who's who and to find out where the leverages of powers were in order to do your job, when meeting Mr. Boban did you ask him to explain to you how this self-styled government of Herceg-Bosna functioned, what it entailed, where it was located, who were the personalities, you know, what municipalities were included, if any, how were the municipalities governed, who was in charge of the military, to what -- what role he played? Did any of those questions pop up during this meeting or any other meeting for that matter with Mr. Boban, the most important person that you were interviewing?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult to obtain information from Mr. Boban to put it mildly, but he would spend a lot -- a significant amount of time talking about what the -- the EC should do for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But, see, that's not the answer.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the answer to your question is no, I did not get that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You see, we'll get along much better if you just cut to the quick, answer my question --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's important to put a picture on the whole thing, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm not cutting you off.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm sort of like a military man too when I'm in court, I like a direct answer, okay, and I'm sure your superiors have told you that before: Give it to me straight. So the answer is you meet with this important person and you don't ask him to explain to you what the self-styled government is. Instead, you're running around thereafter trying to figure it out.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying it.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're saying it. I'm saying I might have asked him but I didn't get the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, before you said, no, I didn't ask him. That's the answer that you gave.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now you're back-sliding?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not back-sliding at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. This is now degenerating into an argument, again, and the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- said what he said and I think counsel has mischaracterised it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree. The transcript speaks for itself. He indicated quite clearly that he did not ask Mr. Boban. I'll accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No he, did not so indicate, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. Mr. Karnavas, before we proceed, Commandant, I want to go back to your hearing with Mr. Spork, your interview with Mr. Spork. We know that you answered the questions put to you by the interviewer for about two days and the cross-examination has to do with your answers when Mr. Spork interviewed you in Dublin, in the headquarters of the army. Did he have a laptop with him or did he ask you questions which he would then note on a document and did he then record your answers? How did this take place? Was it a conversation and then he just noted your answers, he wrote down your answers? Or did he ask you a question and then he typed in your answers into his computer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I remember, Your Honour, he had a laptop computer which he used to put the answers into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So he put questions to you. You would then answer those questions. And he used his laptop to type the answers into the laptop and at the end of the two-day period what you spent with him, did he print out a document that was supposed to contain the answers that you provided to the questions put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So this document and everyone has it, it's a 20-page document, you signed on the 26th of May, 2004, and counsel asked you a minute ago whether you had re-read a document in fact this document. Have you re-read this document carefully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I re-read it over this weekend, Your Honour, or last weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This weekend, but I'm not talking about the past weekend. I'm talking about the 26th of May, 2004. On the 26th of May, 2004, you signed this document. So Mr. Spork put your answers into his computer and printed out the final document which you then signed and he also signed since it consists of 19 pages or -- 19 pages on which we have his signature too. So after you had signed the document did you read or did you re-read the 20 pages? And I'm referring to the 26th of May, 2004? Did you read the entire 20-page document before signing it on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And as far as you can remember, how much time did you need to read through the 20 pages? It takes a certain amount of time. Were you alone in your office when you re-read it, was Mr. Spork sitting next to you, and did he give you a pen to sign the document with once you had re-read it? Do you remember how this took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my memory, I think Mr. Spork was in the same room with me as I read the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And this document is a document that you re-read this weekend. That's what you said just a minute ago. And that's when you realised that this document contained certain things that did not in fact correspond to the reality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before I came here, Your Honour, I gave some consideration to the events of 1992 when I was in Bosnia and because I -- it was on my mind for -- when I returned from Afghanistan four weeks ago, I gave consideration to the events of 1992, and those changes are as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Karnavas, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just to follow up on that series of questions, did Mr. Spork leave you with a copy of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did. He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to where we were, you go on to say on -- I'm going to press you a little bit here, in paragraph 37 you say: "I attended a number of meetings of the Presidency of the self-proclaimed Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I noticed during the meetings that Mr. Prlic was the most significant personality at these meetings. Even though Mr. Boban would chair the meeting, he had very little input into the deliberations." Now, I want to stop and pause over the word "Presidency". You say you were present at a number of meetings of the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. You stand by that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Where were these meetings of the Presidency held?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can remember, they were in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who were the members of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Boban, Mr. Prlic, and other -- other people who I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What were their titles if you can remember that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was the substance that was being discussed? And I take it you must have taken copious notes and passed it on to your superiors of which we would have these lovely reports?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I cannot remember what the subject matter was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, did you ever ask, for instance, Mr. Prlic, who you indicated yesterday and you said so in your -- in your statement that he was open to wherever you wanted to see him, he never declined --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- not to see you, he never declined to answer any of your questions. Did you ever ask him what the function of this Presidency was with respect to this self-styled government given that one of your missions was there to find out about the political and military powers of leverage?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chances are, Counsel, that I did ask him but again, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So -- so maybe yes, maybe no?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course had you asked that question, and had Mr. Boban not answered the question, would you have asked Mr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- expand on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that it was very difficult to get any information from Mr. Boban hence perhaps the - for lack of a better term and I don't mean to be disrespectful - ignorance on your part as far as how this self-styled government of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna functioned and how it was structured, okay? So my question is: If you could not get any answers from Mr. Boban because he seemed to be elusive, did you ask Mr. Prlic? It's either a yes, no --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you don't recall whether you asked Mr. Prlic about this -- these meetings of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yet you sit here today, not knowing who attended, and you -- and you put into your -- and you put in your statement when you spoke to Mr. Spork, who obviously knows what the Presidency is having been an investigator on this case for many, many, many years, okay, how is it that you knew that this was -- that these were meetings of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm going to object. This is -- this issue of the Presidency meetings, it wasn't raised in the direct examination, so it's not a part of the witness's evidence as far as I know. Now, if we want to tender the statement into evidence so that counsel can cross-examine the witness on everything in the statement, those things which were raised on the direct examination as well as those things that weren't, that's fine, but it seems to me to be having it both ways. If he's going to cross-examine the witness on the basis of a statement that he didn't even testify about in his direct examination, well, let's just tender the statement itself into evidence and then -- then the Trial Chamber will have -- will have it all, but I think that what's happening here is a bit unfair. He's cross-examining the witness about something that he didn't testify about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I respond, Mr. President? First all, all of these questions go to the gentleman's credibility, and therefore, they're fair game. They're not just merely outside the scope of direct examination because Mr. Stringer brought this gentleman here and asked him questions. Now I'm entitled to attack his credibility, his knowledge, his memory. Mr. Stringer told us today and apologised that he had learned about this diagram which supposedly was mentioned as a map. These are all relevant issues. They go to challenging the gentleman's memory and veracity. Now, if Mr. Stringer wanted the statement in he could have tendered the statement in or he could have gone into the statement. He could have gone into other areas. I don't know what his strategy is, neither do I care, but this is proper cross-examination, and they can't bring a witness here and expect you to listen to him on direct and then there be no cross concerning issues where obviously the gentleman has lapses of memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My reply, Mr. President, is this: The witness's evidence is his testimony. Now, if we're going to make the witness's evidence also his witness statement, all 24 pages of it, that's fine, and I will tender it, and that way the Trial Chamber will have both the statement and the witness's responses about the statement to issues which were not raised in the direct examination. So that's what I'm going to propose to do, is to tender the entire statement and that way we can have a full record of the witness's responses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, first of all, let me remind the Trial Chamber that if the Prosecutor does that, he is reopening direct examination. I don't want to give him a lesson on evidence, but obviously I'm entitled to go to portions of the statement for purposes of impeachment without introducing the entire statement. He knows that. He's an experienced trial lawyer, both prosecution and defence. So he knows the rules of evidence and I'm entitled to go into areas and I'm entitled to ask him questions of which he spoke to the Prosecution about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, through your questions you're testing the credibility of the witness, and in doing so within the framework of this test you are trying to find out whether he had any knowledge about the functioning of the HVO, the Presidency, Mr. Mate Boban, and you wish to question him on meetings of the Presidency. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during that period of time did you learn anything -- I mean, you mention in your statement and you probably talked to the Prosecutor about this during the weekend when you were going over your statement, about the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. Did conversations with respect to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan come up during your conversation with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from being in the field during that period of time, you would have learned of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now when you say, "we were aware of it", that's sort of the collective "we". Might I ask whether you, Commandant Ray Lane, was aware of it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not formally briefed by ECMM on it, but I became aware of it -- of its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now when you say you were not formally briefed, is there a difference between briefed and formally briefed?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally briefed as in brought back to the regional centre in Split and briefed on the contents of the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they -- did they ever send you the plan and say because you know I understand it was in English as well, it was available in English, both Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen being anglophones, did they ever provide you with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan so at least you could take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ask for it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you're telling us that during the period from January, February, March 1993, which was the period when the Vance-Owen Plan was in existence and was known, you who were meeting on the ground of the head of state of a self-styled country, Mr. Mate Boban, your own hierarchy never provided you with any information about the contents of this plan, no information at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in January, February, and March of 1993, as you're aware I spent most of my time in Gornji Vakuf in that difficult situation there. As I said before, we were working 13, 14 hours a day. So my -- my job at that time was to try and control the situation in Gornji Vakuf, and the Vance-Owen Peace Plan was left to the good offices of Mr. Bousseau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... That if we wanted to find out exactly what his understanding was of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan and what if any discussions he held with the key players at the time he would be the one that we would need to bring over here?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bousseau is an important man, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you -- he's an ambassador; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He would have been aware of the plan?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I'm -- absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I think yesterday you said at times you were accompanying him at the meetings?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'm going to get to that one meeting on the 25th, but did you ever ask him hey, ambassador -- and I take it he was a nice guy?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very lovely, open?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was French.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, so he was open to you?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good man. And did you ever say to him, ambassador, explain to me this Vance-Owen Peace Plan, you know, just so I know, because --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- some of the folks that I supervise might want to know, so in case it pops up. Did you ever ask him that question?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a recollection that he discussed the Vance -- the Vance-Owen Peace Plan with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you didn't grasp it at the time and that's why you can't elucidate on that?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat that in January, February of 1993 I was extremely busy in my role in Gornji Vakuf, and it -- you need to understand that this wasn't a part-time job up there. This was full time, requiring all my energies and direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the events in Gornji Vakuf began sort of -- I mean, there were some incidents as early as 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in the first week of January was there any incidents up there?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it's my understanding that the events in Gornji Vakuf had nothing to do with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. Would that be your understanding as well?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please make breaks between questions and answers. Otherwise its impossible for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'm trying to find this. There is a lovely paragraph here that it's -- I'm not -- I'm not quite sure. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpreters are asking you to slow down. I think yesterday we beat all records. There were 130 pages of transcript. If we continue at this pace we're going to set another record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you said here on paragraph 96 that: "The purpose of this offensive was to consolidate the Croatian position and obtain as much ground as possible before any possible peace plan. Even though we were aware of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan at the time, it is unlikely that this operation was affected by this plan." Now, those were your words back then; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So it would seem to me at least in reading this particular paragraph what you're -- what you're saying is that this offensive operation, and you indicated - and correct me if I'm wrong, I certainly don't want to put words in your mouth - that the operation occurred prior to the announcement of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan or prior to January 15th that one had nothing to do with the other. Is that what you're trying to say here?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was your understanding then?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At the time, that is when you were in the field. That was your understanding in 2004. That remains to be your understanding in 2007.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in your statement, I just wanted to cover this very briefly to make sure I don't forget about it, you indicated that -- and this is on paragraph 102 of your statement, you had indicated that on -- that you were present at a meeting where -- with Mr. Prlic and the ambassador, and this would have been on January 25th, 1993. That's what you told --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- the investigator back then; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, he showed you a document?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And based on that document you said and I quote: "I was shown by the investigator a copy of the ECMM daily monitoring activity of the 25th January 1993." And then the investigator has a little insert, and then you go on to say: "I was present during this meeting and I can confirm that Mr. Prlic expressed his view that he had ordered the HVO commander in Gornji Vakuf to stop all attacks immediately." This -- the document is a true and accurate reflection of what occurred. That's what you told the investigator at the time.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we're going to go step-by-step. Over the weekend when you met with the Prosecutor, having had time to reflect in between your missions, you realised that you were not present at the meeting of the 25th.

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so therefore you cannot vouch, assuming that's what the document shows, and of course, there were two documents if you recall yesterday --

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- where I intervened. One was, I believe it was Prosecution document - let me think about it - 1303?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's where the Prosecution skipped over. And then there was a document of 1309 and that's the one that he wanted you to go to?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because one summarises, albeit with some liberties, might I say, the events of the 25th. Now -- so what you're telling us is at this point in time is that, one, when you gave the statement in Dublin, in your office with the Prosecutor where you had all the time to reflect and also time to read and look at documents that were shown to you by the investigator, your recollection was that you were there and of course now we know thankfully, and we appreciate this and we're grateful, now we know that what you told the -- the Prosecutor -- the investigator for the Prosecution was not correct and actually the document that he did show you you cannot vouch for its accuracy or its veracity; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Might I ask, might I ask, the technique that was used, the technique in trying to get information from you. Did the Prosecutor -- because this might assist us a little bit. In other words, did he say, "Mr. Lane, what, if any, meetings did you attend at the time?" And you scratched your head, maybe looked at some of your own personal documents and said, "Well, I was at these sorts of meeting." Or did he show you and point into particular passages of documents which might be relevant to the Prosecution's theory and said, "Look at this. Look in particular here. See this. Now, tell me, sir, were you at the meeting?" In other words, asking a witness, you know, was the light green or red, and if it was red, then obviously, you know, you might be off base, but what colour was it?

utterances.speaker: RAYMOND LANE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think from what I recollect, a series of events were put in front of me and had I been a part of that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to show you a couple of documents, and I mention this because I'm wondering whether the Prosecution shared with you this document during the briefing session or maybe even if Mr. Spork had shared this document that came from -- at least this was -- this was a Prosecution document, and I'm referring to document P 01293.
